1. In the criminal revision petition under Section 397 Cr.P.C., the petitioners challenged order on charge dated 01.08.2022 and charges framed on 09.09.2022, and charge amended on 07.02.2023 (In short 'the impugned orders') in FIR No. 219/2017 under Section 498A/406/506/34 IPC registered at PS Roop Nagar whereby the trial Court discharged the accused No. 5, namely, Kusum Agarwal and the accused No. 6, namely, Saurav Agarwal from offences under Section 498A/406/506/34 IPC, and framed charges under Section 498A/506/34 IPC against the petitioner No. 1 and 2, and the accused No. 1, namely, Nitin Agarwal and the accused No. 3, namely, Nikhil Agarwal and under Section 406/34 IPC against the petitioner No. 1 and the accused No. 1.

sentences.text: . The complainant was married to the accused No. 1 on 25.02.2011.
She filed a complaint with PS Roop Nagar on 10.10.2016 on averments that the accused persons subjected her to cruelty to meet their unlawful demands.
In the complaint, she stated that the accused persons had taken possession of stridhan and other valuable articles.
She stated that the accused persons demanded amount several times.
She also made allegations of physical assault.
The dispute could not be amicably settled and thereafter, the case FIR was registered on 14.09.2017 which eventually culminated into filing of charge-sheet on 22.04.2019.
The trial Court taken cognizance of offences and summoned the accused persons including the petitioners.

sentences.text: The trial Court, vide order dated 01.08.2022, formed an opinion that the material on record discloses commission of offences under Section 498A/506/34 IPC against the accused No. 1, the petitioner No. 1, the accused No. 3 and the petitioner No. 2 and offence under Section 406 IPC against the accused No. 1 and the petitioner No. 1.
Consequently, the trial Court framed requisite charges on 07.02.2023.
4. Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned orders, the petitioners filed the criminal revision petition.

5. I have heard Ms. Shubra Mendiratta, Advocate for the petitioners and Mr. Akshay Arora,
Advocate for the complainant and perused written arguments filed by the complainant and examined trial Court record.
6. The accused No. 1 is husband of the complainant.
The petitioner No. 1 (the accused No. 2) is mother- in-law and the accused No. 3 is her brother-in-law (devar).
Crl. Rev. No. 609/2022 Mrs. Veena Agarwal & Anr. vs. State Page No. 2 of 10 7.

entities.text: Crl. Rev. No. 609/2022 Mrs. Veena Agarwal & Anr. vs. State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The accused No. 4 was uncle-in-law who expired on 27.04.2021.
The accused No. 5 is aunt-in-law and the accused No. 6 is son of the accused No. 4 and 5.

The accused No. 7 is sister-in-law (nanad)
of the complainant.
8. Ld.
Counsel for the petitioners contended that the impugned orders are patently erroneous.
She contended that the trial Court did not appreciate that the petitioner No. 1 is a senior citizen and the petitioner No. 2 is married sister-in-law.
She contended that the petitioner No. 2 seldom visits her parental house.
She contended that the petitioner No. 2 never made any dowry demand or instigated anyone.
She contended that the complainant voluntarily left matrimonial house on 19.06.2014.
She contended that the complainant filed the complaint after a period of two and half years.
She contended that there is no allegation against the petitioners.
She contended that the allegations are general, non-specific and omnibus.
She contended that the complainant has neither mentioned date nor time of the incident.
She contended that the petitioner No. 1 is in her advance age and she is immobile.
She contended that the trial Court did not consider the report of Family Welfare Committee (FWC) and IO ASI Satish Kumar.
She contended that the complainant has not furnished any receipt pertaining to purchase of any jewellery articles or the source of amount for purchasing the said articles.
She contended that there is no PCR call, MLC or police complaint regarding the assault alleged by the complainant.

She contended that there is no material disclosing prima facie commission of offences under Section 498A, 406 and 506 IPC against the petitioner No.
1 and 498A and 506 IPC against the petitioner No. 2.
Crl. Rev. No. 609/2022 Mrs. Veena Agarwal & Anr. vs. State Page No. 3 of 10 9.
Ld. Counsel for the complainant contended that there are specific allegations against the petitioners.
He referred the averments made in the complaint.

He contended that the trial Court considered the law applicable to the cases of this nature at the stage of charge and framed charges Mrs. Veena Agarwal vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82025696/
2 after due application of mind.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He contended that the Court cannot conduct a mini trial at this stage.
He contended that sufficiency of the material cannot be evaluated at this stage.
He contended that there is no material infirmity, illegality or manifest perversity in the impugned orders.

10. The scope of interference by a revisional Court at the stage of charge was delineated in the judgment of Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander and Another, (2012) 9 SCC 460, as under:
"12.....the revisional jurisdiction can be invoked where the decisions under challenge are grossly erroneous, there is no compliance with the provisions of law, the finding recorded is based on no evidence, material evidence is ignored or judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or perversely.

entities.text: Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander and Another, (2012) 9 SCC 460
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These are not exhaustive classes, but are merely indicative.
Each case would have to be determined on its own merits.
16. The abovestated principles clearly show that inherent as well as revisional jurisdiction should be exercised cautiously.

If the jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code in relation to quashing of an FIR is circumscribed by the factum and caution aforenoticed, in that event, the revisional jurisdiction, particularly while dealing with framing of a charge, has to be even more limited.
18.....Basically, the power is required to be exercised so that justice is done and there is no abuse of power by the court.
Merely an apprehension or suspicion of the same would not be a sufficient ground for interference in such cases.

20. The jurisdiction of the court under Section 397 can be exercised so as to examine the correctness, legality or propriety of an order passed by the trial court or the inferior court, as the case may be.
Crl. Rev. No. 609/2022 Mrs. Veena Agarwal & Anr. vs. State Page No. 4 of 10

Though the section does not specifically use the expression "prevent abuse of process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice", the jurisdiction under Section 397 is a very limited one.
The legality, propriety or correctness of an order passed by a court is the very foundation of exercise of jurisdiction under Section 397 but ultimately it also requires justice to be done.

The jurisdiction could be exercised where there is palpable error, non- compliance with the provisions of law, the decision is completely erroneous or where the judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily....."
11. It would be appropriate to have a glimpse of legal principles governing the issue of charge.

12. In Union of India vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal, AIR 1979 SC 366, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India enumerated the scope and ambit of Section 227 Cr.P.C., as under:
"10.

entities.text: Union of India vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal, AIR 1979 SC 366
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, on a consideration of the authorities mentioned above, the following principles emerge:
Mrs. Veena Agarwal vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82025696/
3

entities.text: Veena Agarwal vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (1) That the Judge while considering the question of framing the charges under section 227 of the Code has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out:

(2) Where the materials placed before the Court disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained the Court will be, fully justified in framing a charge and proceeding with the trial.
(3) The test to determine a prima facie case would naturally depend upon the facts of each case and it is difficult to lay down a rule of universal application.

By and large however if two views are equally possible and the Judge is satisfied that the evidence produced before him while giving rise to some suspicion but not grave suspicion against the accused, he will be fully within his right to discharge the accused.

(4) That in exercising his jurisdiction under section 227 of the Code the Judge which under the present Code is a senior and experienced Judge cannot act merely as a Post office or a mouth-piece of the prosecution, but has to consider the broad Crl. Rev. No. 609/2022 Mrs. Veena Agarwal & Anr.
vs. State Page No. 5 of 10 probabilities of the case, the total effect of the evidence and the documents produced before the Court, any basic infirmities appearing in the case and so on.
This however does not mean that the Judge should make a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial."

13. In Saranya vs. Bharathi and Another, (2021) 8 SCC 583, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India delineated principles governing framing of charge, as under:
"11.....it is observed and held that at the stage of framing of charges, the Court has to consider the material only with a view to find out if there is a ground for 'presuming'
that the accused had committed the offence.

entities.text: Saranya vs. Bharathi and Another, (2021) 8 SCC 583
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is observed and held that at that stage,
the High Court is required to evaluate the material and documents on record with a view to finding out if the facts emerging therefrom, taken at their face value, disclose the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence or offences.

It is further observed and held that at this stage the High Court is not required to appreciate the evidence on record and consider the allegations on merits and to find out on the basis of the evidence recorded the accused chargesheeted or against whom the charge is framed is likely to be convicted or not."
14.

In State Through Deputy Superintendent of Police vs. R. Soundirarasu etc., 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1150, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held, as under:
"53.

entities.text: State Through Deputy Superintendent of Police vs. R. Soundirarasu etc., 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1150
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The primary consideration at the stage of framing of charge is the test of existence of a prima facie case, and at this stage, the probative value of materials on record is not to be gone into.

Mrs. Veena Agarwal vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82025696/
4 55.....The obligation to discharge the accused under Section 239 arises when "the Magistrate considers the charge against the accused to be groundless".....
57.....at that stage, the Court has to form a presumptive opinion as to the existence of the factual ingredients constituting the offence alleged and it is not expected to go deep into the probative value of the materials on record.....

entities.text: Veena Agarwal vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus the word 'groundless', as interpreted by this Court, means that there is no ground for presuming that the accused has committed an offence.

72. The real test for determining whether the charge should be considered groundless under Section 239 of the CrPC is that whether the materials are such that even if unrebutted make out no case whatsoever, the accused should be discharged under Section 239 of the CrPC.

The trial court will have to consider, whether the materials relied upon by the prosecution against the applicant herein for the purpose of framing of the charge, if unrebutted, make out any case at all."

15. In Vikram Johar vs. State of Uttar Pradesh, (2019) 14 SCC 207, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India emphasized need of application of judicial mind to determine the potentiality of the case for a trial,
as under:
"18.

entities.text: Vikram Johar vs. State of Uttar Pradesh, (2019) 14 SCC 207
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is, thus clear that while considering the discharge application, the Court is to exercise its judicial mind to determine whether a case for trial has been made out or not.

It is true that in such proceedings, the Court is not to hold the mini trial by marshalling the evidence."
16.
The issue before this Court is whether there is material on record disclosing prima facie commission of offences against the petitioners.

17. On examination of the allegations made in the complaint, it is evident that there are allegations against the petitioner No. 2 that she asked the complainant's mother to arrange an amount of Rs.
5,00,000/- for meeting expenses of honeymoon.
There are allegations that the petitioner No. 2 misbehaved with the complainant's parents for not making payment as 'milni' on the occasion of first holi.
There are allegations that the petitioner No. 2 misbehaved with the complainant's father on the occasion of 'rakshabandhan' for not giving expensive gifts to her.
Crl. Rev. No. 609/2022 Mrs. Veena Agarwal & Anr. vs. State Page No. 7 of 10 18.

entities.text: Crl. Rev. No. 609/2022 Mrs. Veena Agarwal & Anr. vs. State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are allegations of misbehaviour and use of offending words by the petitioner No. 2 against the complainant.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the trial Court had no material to frame charges against the petitioner No. 2.

Mrs. Veena Agarwal vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82025696/
5 19.

entities.text: Veena Agarwal vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, there are specific allegations pertaining to entrustment of stridhan to the petitioner No. 1.

There are allegations of repeated demands of amount and valuable articles as well as verbal and physical abuse against the petitioner No. 1.
20.

In Sheoraj Singh Ahlawat and Others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another, (2013) 11 SCC 476,
Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held, as under:
"12.....A plain reading of the above would show that the court trying the case can direct discharge only for reasons to be recorded by it and only if it considers the charge against the accused to be groundless.

entities.text: Sheoraj Singh Ahlawat and Others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another, (2013) 11 SCC 476
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
13. Section 240 of the Code provides for framing of a charge if, upon consideration of the police report and the documents sent therewith and making such examination, if any, of the accused as the Magistrate thinks necessary, the Magistrate is of the opinion that there is ground for presuming that the accused has committed an offence triable under Chapter XIX, which such Magistrate is competent to try and which can be adequately punished by him."
21. The trial Court taken note of the allegations made in the complaint and statements of the other witnesses, as well as relevant judgments applicable to the cases of this nature and thereafter, the trial Court formed an opinion that there is sufficient material for framing of charges under Section 498A/406/506/34 IPC against the petitioner No. 1 and charges under Section 498A/506/34 IPC against the petitioner No. 2.
The perusal of order demonstrates application of judicial mind by the trial Court.
Crl. Rev. No. 609/2022 Mrs. Veena Agarwal & Anr. vs. State Page No. 8 of 10 22.

entities.text: Crl. Rev. No. 609/2022 Mrs. Veena Agarwal & Anr. vs. State Page No. 8 of 10
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it cannot be said that the charges against the petitioners are groundless and there was no material for framing of charges against them.
23. The conciliation proceedings before the Family Welfare Committee and CAW Cell are confidential and they cannot be filed or relied in these proceedings.
24. Authenticity, credibility and sufficiency of material is alien to the stage of framing of charge.
25. This Court does not find any material illegality, manifest perversity or jurisdictional error in the impugned orders.

26. As regards medical condition of the petitioner No. 1 and inconvenience faced by the petitioner No. 2 in attending trial of the case, it would be appropriate that they be permanently exempted from their personal attendance subject to filing of an affidavit that they will not dispute the evidence recorded in their absence and they will not dispute their identity.

CONCLUSION:
